learningObjectives: Load and persist named XML resources.
Select an existing container and insert new elements.
Identify intended records and verify independent expected values.
Distinguish resource assertions from persisted-file verification.

elements.text: Open/Create XML file loads data into a resource. Use its name consistently for each step operating on that resource. Select the intended existing container; Insert creates the new element and its structure. Input can modify existing XML elements; it is not restricted to configuration fields such as Filepath.

Save XML file writes a resource to disk. Its optional Filepath selects a different destination from the connected source; if omitted for a resource loaded from a file, saving targets that connected file. For a newly created resource without a connected file, do not assume there is an original path to overwrite.

Independent guidance: use a full disposable output path and inspect the intended destination, permissions and overwrite risk. A different filename is not an absolute preservation guarantee if another file already occupies that destination. Do not infer directory-creation behavior from an unverified claim.

Independent example: among repeated Product elements, select the intended parent and use a unique Id constraint to identify Product 635 before checking its expected fields. Inspect uniqueness; a Constraint is not guaranteed to make duplicate IDs unique. Other supported selection mechanisms may also apply.

Verify XML can check resource content with XPath and explicit expected results. Configure namespaces when the expression needs them. A resource check proves the current resource state; to check persistence, save to a disposable output and reload that file into a separately named resource before asserting.
Load a disposable XML copy, insert one new record, inspect resource values and save to a deliberate output path. Academy Exercise 12a was inaccessible; no local Tosca execution was performed.

Reload the saved output, locate the intended unique record and assert independent expected values. Add checks for duplicates, namespaces and malformed input appropriate to the contract. Academy Exercise 12b and course examination coverage are not certified.

examPitfalls.title: Mismatching resource identity
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Editing one resource but saving or checking another.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the intended name consistently across related steps.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing existing and new elements
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Inserting a second parent instead of selecting the existing container.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Select the existing target; Insert adds new elements; Input modifies existing ones.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming identification is unique
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using a duplicated Id constraint without inspecting results.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Define and verify uniqueness rather than relying on the name of the field.

examPitfalls.title: Checking only the resource after saving
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming in-memory assertions prove persisted output.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Save explicitly, reload the destination and assert its content.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In this insertion scenario, which mode selects an existing parent container before adding a new child?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Select identifies the existing target; Insert adds the new child.

optionExplanations.A: Insert would add a new element rather than select the existing parent.
optionExplanations.C: Verify checks a value rather than choosing this insertion target.
optionExplanations.D: Buffer captures data instead of selecting the intended container.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A resource was loaded from an XML file and remains connected to it. What does Save XML file target when optional Filepath is omitted?
practiceQuiz.hint: This scenario explicitly has a connected file.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The optional path chooses a different destination; omission uses the connected file.

optionExplanations.A: The optional path is not always mandatory in this scenario.
optionExplanations.B: This is the documented connected-file target.
optionExplanations.C: No random filename behavior is established.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Products have unique Id values. How can a verification target Product 635 among repeated Products?

options.text: Verify every field and assume automatic identity selection.
Constrain Id to 635, then Verify the intended remaining fields.
Buffer the Id and assume that selects the record.

practiceQuiz.rationale: A constraint identifies the intended record under the uniqueness assumption.

optionExplanations.A: Assertions alone do not establish this selection.
optionExplanations.B: This scopes selection to the stated unique identity.
optionExplanations.D: Capturing a value alone does not constrain the search.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Related steps must edit and persist the same named XML resource. What must their resource references do?

options.text: Use a different name in every step.
Appear only in the Save step.

practiceQuiz.hint: Resource names identify the working data.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Consistent references ensure the steps target the intended resource; deliberate copying can use different named resources.

optionExplanations.A: This preserves the intended identity across these steps.
optionExplanations.C: Load and manipulation also need the intended resource identity.
optionExplanations.D: Blank names do not specify this intended resource.

quickRecap.value: Open/Create XML file uses a named resource.
Omitted path uses a connected source; explicit path selects a destination.
Select existing target; Insert new elements; Input existing elements.
Identify intended records and assert explicit expected values.
Related operations reference the same intended resource.
Reload the output to verify saved content; course completion is not certified here.
